pr_title: Allow --org parameter in lieu of a repo context for rulesets, add current_user_can_bypass to rs view
pr_body:
Fixes #7699 and adds one more REST API field to the `view` subcommand.

#### Repo context/`--org` flag
A repo context is not necessary if the `--org` flag is used for ruleset subcommands, so this prevents the "repo not found" error from being thrown if the `--org` flag is provided outside of a repo. It also expands the tests to ensure nothing is being missed with `repoI` potentially being undefined. I don't really like this way of fixing this because it relies on `repoI` just not being touched when it shouldn't be, but I think refactoring to avoid that would make the code pretty difficult to read. Open to suggestions though if I'm missing something simple.

#### `current_user_can_bypass` REST API field
This PR also adds in the new `current_user_can_bypass` REST API field, which indicates whether the user making the request can bypass the ruleset. This is only returned by the REST API when queried with a repo context, so it will not be returned when using the `--org` flag, in which case I hide it completely. The three (current) possible display values will end up looking like:

```
You can bypass: never
You can bypass: pull requests only
You can bypass: always
```

issue_context.title: Ruleset subcommands shouldn't require being in a repo if using the `--org` flag
issue_context.body: All 3 of the subcommands for `gh ruleset` currently require a repo context. This is expected for `rs check`, but `rs list` and `rs view` don't need the repo context if the `--org` flag is used as that provides all necessary context. I'll open a PR soon to correct this.

review_comments: Perhaps I am not well versed enough in rulesets but this sounds a bit off when read out loud. Is there another way we can phrase this? Or perhaps just shorten it to `Bypass:` similar to the other properties.

I debated this too, but I'm honestly not sure what makes the most sense here. There are two different bypass fields:
- The general list of all roles/teams that can bypass the ruleset (already displayed in the `view` subcommand)
- This new one, whether the user making the request can bypass the ruleset.
  - It basically has the server check whether the current user is a member of any of the roles/teams that are allowed to bypass, otherwise consumers would need to manually query each one to see if the user is a member of any of them.

The full bypass list is labeled "Bypass List" in the output, and I labeled this one "You can bypass" to make it clearer that it's whether you, the person making the request, can bypass the ruleset. Otherwise it may seem like it's a global rule that applies to everyone.

That all makes sense to me. I don't know if I have any better ideas. It is kind of interesting that this new field does not tell us which role the current user belongs to that allows them to bypass the ruleset. That would make displaying the information easier I think.

Agreed, that would be nice, but the server-side code would require a bunch of refactoring to support that and it was out of scope for this. I can tweak the wording if you'd like, otherwise I think this is ready.
